facts.fact: The central bank (BCRG) carried the NimbaPay national instant payment system, launched in Conakry on 22 July 2026 and connecting banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions, with transfers possible from go-live.

systems.owner: BCRG, implemented by Guineenne de Monetique

GIN.note: Nothing on consumer protection rules or redress.
Cross-border payments are named only as a later phase of NimbaPay, with no pilot, licence or rule stated.
Nothing on government payments to people.
The 36% access rate in 2024 is given by the governor with no survey named, so it is not recorded as a survey share.

facts.fact: The BCRG governor said financial access rose from 4% in 2011 to nearly 36% in 2024 thanks notably to the rise of electronic money, which implies e-money in service.

NimbaPay, in service from its 22 July 2026 launch, lets clients of connected institutions make instant, interoperable transfers between accounts regardless of their bank or financial service provider, across banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions.
NimbaPay is described as Guinea's national instant payment system, connecting banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions, in service from 22 July 2026.

systems.owner: BCRG, implemented by Guineenne de Monetique

GIN.note: Payments to public administrations are named only as a later NimbaPay phase, with no pilot or contract stated.
